scope: Post-2022 journal publications on credit-card/financial fraud detection; official publisher records, primary full text and institutional bibliographic records.
policy: Literature claims are attributed to authors, not independently replicated. No literature metric should be used as a direct benchmark without matching datasets, splits, prevalence, threshold and evaluation protocol.

records.title: A systematic review of literature on credit card cyber fraud detection using machine and deep learning
records.datasets: Review of heterogeneous datasets in 181 studies from 2019-2021; not a new controlled IEEE-CIS experiment.
records.verified_claim: Synthesizes machine/deep learning approaches and identifies class imbalance, changing fraud patterns and practical constraints.
records.limitations: Publication is from 2023, but review coverage ends in 2021. Does not establish the best model for IEEE-CIS.
records.verification: All authors, date, title, venue and DOI appear in the primary full-text header; review scope appears in abstract and survey methodology.

records.title: A Survey on GAN Techniques for Data Augmentation to Address the Imbalanced Data Issues in Credit Card Fraud Detection
records.datasets: Survey of fraud-data augmentation studies; no single newly evaluated IEEE-CIS dataset.
records.verified_claim: Reviews GAN augmentation variants and discusses instability, mode collapse, sample quality and inconsistent evaluation.
records.relevance: Places SMOTE within the broader augmentation literature and motivates cautious interpretation of synthetic samples.
records.limitations: Survey findings do not prove GAN superiority under this project's split or categorical representation.
records.verification: Publisher record supplies both authors, DOI, venue, volume, pages and publication date; institutional repository corroborates.

records.title: Enhancing Financial Fraud Detection through Addressing Class Imbalance Using Hybrid SMOTE-GAN Techniques
records.datasets: European cardholders' September 2013 transactions, 284,807 rows with 492 fraud cases; not IEEE-CIS.
records.verified_claim: Compares SMOTE, GAN and hybrid augmentation using FNN, CNN and FNN+CNN; generation is described as training-only.
records.relevance: Close empirical precedent for ANN oversampling comparisons and configurable hyperparameters.
records.limitations: Section 3.1 describes scaling before the split, raising preprocessing-leakage concerns. Different dataset and fraud prevalence prevent direct numerical comparison.
records.verification: Publisher header supplies complete metadata; Sections 3.1-3.4 establish dataset and models. Protocol caveat is an inference from Section 3.1's stated order.

records.title: Data Leakage and Deceptive Performance: A Critical Examination of Credit Card Fraud Detection Methodologies
records.type: critical methodological review with empirical MLP case study
records.datasets: European credit-card fraud benchmark: 284,807 transactions, 492 fraud cases; not IEEE-CIS.
records.verified_claim: Deliberately contrasts faulty preprocessing/resampling protocols with corrected evaluation to demonstrate inflated apparent performance.
records.relevance: Direct justification for training-only resampling, untouched holdouts, temporal analysis and reporting precision alongside recall.
records.limitations: Case-study findings concern this benchmark and specified experiments. The paper's criticisms of other work are author assessments, not an independent replication by this project.
records.verification: Official publisher PDF first page supplies authors, date, venue and DOI; Section 2.1 supplies dataset; methodology/results describe leakage experiment.

records.title: Intelligent approach to detecting online fraudulent trading with solution for imbalanced data in fintech forensics
records.datasets: Reports an IEEE-CIS validation in Experiment 8; primary data availability statement otherwise points broadly to Kaggle datasets.
records.verified_claim: Combines ABC sampling, rule filtering, K-means and KNN; reports a separate IEEE-CIS evaluation without augmentation.
records.relevance: Same-dataset discussion of imbalance mitigation, while method differs from the project's ANN comparisons.
records.limitations: Experiment 8 uses future-tense protocol wording and lacks exact holdout IDs, temporal boundary and feature mapping needed for reproducible comparison. Treat reported results as contextual, not directly comparable.
records.verification: Primary full-text header verifies metadata; proposed-model section verifies method; Experiment 8 explicitly identifies IEEE-CIS.

records.title: Uncertainty-aware credit card fraud detection using deep learning
records.datasets: Publisher indexed section identifies IEEE-CIS. The 2021 primary preprint reports a balanced 41,326-row Vesta/IEEE-CIS-derived sample with 385 features; this exact sample detail was not independently verified against closed journal full text.
records.verified_claim: Proposes Monte Carlo dropout, neural ensembles and ensemble Monte Carlo dropout to estimate predictive uncertainty.
records.relevance: Closest neural-network IEEE-CIS reference; supports calibration/uncertainty discussion and future work.
records.limitations: Journal full text unavailable in this environment. Do not transfer precise preprint experimental numbers to the journal citation. Preprint has 10 authors; journal institutional records list 8. Use the 8-author journal metadata for BibTeX.
records.verification: Publisher search record verifies title, DOI, issue date, venue and IEEE-CIS section; two institutional records corroborate eight authors. Full names corroborated by author preprint and reliable bibliographic records. No exact online-publication day claimed.
